title: Exponents & Polynomial Operations
summary: Exponent laws let you multiply, divide, and raise powers, and handle zero and negatives. Polynomials add, subtract, and multiply term by term — including the FOIL pattern and special products like $(a\pm b)^2$ and $(a+b)(a-b)$.

exponent.plain: How many times to multiply the base by itself.

product rule (exponents).plain: Multiply same bases by adding exponents.

quotient rule (exponents).plain: Divide same bases by subtracting exponents.

power rule (exponents).plain: Raise a power to a power by multiplying.

zero exponent.plain: Any nonzero base to the zero is 1.

polynomial.plain: A sum of terms $c\,x^k$ with whole-number exponents.
polynomial.in_class: Add/subtract like terms; multiply by distribution.

concept_sections.heading: Exponent laws
concept_sections.explanation: Combine like bases: add exponents to multiply, subtract to divide, multiply to raise a power to a power. These three rules cover most simplification.

concept_sections.heading: Zero and negative exponents
concept_sections.explanation: A zero exponent gives $1$; a negative exponent means reciprocal. Rewrite negatives as positives by moving the factor across the fraction bar.
math_steps: Move a factor to the other side of the bar to flip the sign.

concept_sections.heading: Adding and subtracting polynomials
concept_sections.explanation: Combine only like terms — same variable and exponent. Line them up and add coefficients; distribute a leading minus carefully.
math_steps: Distribute any subtraction across all terms.

concept_sections.heading: Multiplying polynomials
concept_sections.explanation: Distribute every term of one factor over every term of the other. For two binomials this is FOIL; for larger ones, be systematic.
math_steps: Multiply each term by each term.

concept_sections.heading: Special products
concept_sections.explanation: Memorize $(a+b)^2=a^2+2ab+b^2$, $(a-b)^2=a^2-2ab+b^2$, and $(a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2$. They speed up expansion and later factoring.
math_steps: Square of a sum: middle term $2ab$.
Square of a difference: middle term $-2ab$.

real_world_examples.title: Scientific notation
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Exponent laws multiply and divide numbers written as $c\times10^n$.

real_world_examples.title: Compound area
real_world_examples.scenario: A square garden's side is a binomial length.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Its area $(x+3)^2$ expands with the square-of-a-sum special product.

real_world_examples.title: Computer storage doubling
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Powers of two and the product rule track total growth $2^m\cdot2^n=2^{m+n}$.
